display_name: Read a session's cached context-window occupancy
description: maintenance-verbs M1 (shape (a)). Reads back the cached snapshot report_context_status last wrote for one session. ACCEPTS EITHER ID THE SESSION IS KNOWN BY (GAU-07, 2026-08-18): the LEDGER id the gauge row is keyed on, or the WATCH id peer_list publishes for a watcher-held session, which is resolved internally through the peer binding's stable agent_session_id. Before that fix, enumerating the fleet through peer_list -- the documented way -- made every watcher-held session read as gauge-less even while it was reporting normally. The returned agent_instance_id is always the LEDGER id of the row actually found, with queried_agent_instance_id carrying whatever the caller passed and id_resolution saying which path was taken ('direct', 'resolved_via_binding', or 'unresolved'). The peer_list envelope is unchanged. Fields: model, current_tokens, ceiling, the derived fraction of ceiling, a per-prompt carriage-cost estimate (~10% of current_tokens, the operator's own cached-context-cost arithmetic), whether rotation is due (fraction >= rotation_thresholds.ROTATION_THRESHOLD_FRACTION), and when it was measured. resolved=false (never a raised error) is the expected, stable shape when no report has landed yet for that session — a fresh session pre-first-tick, or (until its own seat-wiring design note is acted on) a host=operator seat. This handler is a trivial state read; it never resolves a transcript path or touches a file itself. Returns cache state as THREE values, not two: true, false, or null for NOT REPORTED — null is never a synonym for a warm cache. Also returns rotation_band and rotation_guidance, DERIVED at read time from the live economic-policy constants (warm bands 150K/200K/300K; cold compares against the measured H of 110,702 tokens), so a policy change never requires backfilling stored rows. When cache state was not reported the band is the WARM one and the null beside it is how the caller can tell. Also returns two reporter-attribution fields, reporter_surface and reporter_generation, saying which copy of the reporting hook wrote the row. Read them BEFORE concluding anything from an absent cache field: several hook copies can be registered at once and only the latest write survives here, so null cache state beside a null or older reporter means a stale copy served that tick — a different fact, with a different fix, from the verbs being undeployed. Both are null when the reporter predates attribution, which identifies that reporter as stale by construction.
embedding_description: Reading back how full a session's context window is, whether its prompt cache is still live, which hook copy last wrote the row, and what the rotation policy says to do now -- keep working, rotate at the next task boundary, at the first safe checkpoint, or immediately. Accepts either the ledger id or the watch id peer_list publishes. Explains itself when no report has landed.

result_processor_customizations.result_description: resolved, resolution_error, agent_instance_id, claude_session_id, model, current_tokens, ceiling, fraction, per_prompt_carriage_estimate_tokens, rotation_due, measured_at. Plus queried_agent_instance_id (the id the caller passed) and id_resolution ('direct', 'resolved_via_binding', 'unresolved'); agent_instance_id is always the LEDGER id of the row that was found, which may differ from the id queried.
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: Lead with resolved — if false, report resolution_error verbatim and stop; never estimate a number in its place. If resolved and rotation_due is true, say so plainly; the operator's checkpoint-and-stop tripwire (~60% of ceiling) is stricter than this verb's own rotation_due flag (0.5), so a caller applying the tripwire should compare fraction directly, not rely on rotation_due alone. When id_resolution is 'resolved_via_binding', the caller queried a watch id and the row was reached through the session's stable agent_session_id -- report the reading normally; that is a successful lookup, not a degraded one.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: A single filtered read on agent_instance_id against the session_context_status cache table.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: missing_argument: agent_instance_id was empty. state_service_unavailable: the state service is not bound. Absence of a cached row is NOT an error — it returns resolved=false in a normal successful result, never a raised failure. ambiguous_agent_session_id: more than one gauge row claims the same stable session id, so the watch-id join cannot say which session was meant -- the verb refuses rather than returning an arbitrary one.
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: For missing_argument, supply the target session's own agent_instance_id (ledger id for a worker, from list_sessions/session_status; a worker/seat's own env-native AGENT_INSTANCE_ID for itself). For ambiguous_agent_session_id, inspect the named rows: two live sessions should never share one agent_session_id, so this indicates duplicate or stale gauge rows to reconcile, not a caller error to retry.
